steps.name: Rus
steps.text: What are you up to this late at night? I could see your torch from a mile away.

steps.name: Worried Pirate
steps.text: Night watch.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You forget we're in a town? No saltfins barging into the camp at night, and the roof above your head isn't getting blown away by a saltstorm.

steps.name: Worried Pirate
steps.text: I know. Just not used to it.

steps.name: Worried Pirate
steps.text: Room's too hot, the bed doesn't shake. I can't sleep.

steps.name: Worried Pirate
steps.text: Besides, something's not right here. That Calificador, Silver, brought us here, but where is he?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Probably just thinks he's too good for us.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: The townsfolk are still on their guard against us. That's why they brought us here at night and hid us in these abandoned shacks.

steps.name: Worried Pirate
steps.text: Aren't we people too? How're we different?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...*sigh*

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Give me the torch. If you're that worried, I'll keep watch.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You get some sleep.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You'll need to get used to being 'civilized'.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I see you're still eating the jerky from your ships.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Señor Javier?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Ah, yes, jerky.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: This kitchen hasn't seen use in quite a while, but Silver had it specially repaired. The utensils should be readily available.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I hear that you've always wanted to be a cook. So why do you not cook when you finally have a proper kitchen?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I just can't. Not today.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Whyever not? Is this still not enough?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: It's enough, I assure you. Never seen so many kitchen tools my whole life.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Why, then?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I insist on knowing, Señor Javier.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: When you cook, it's not the knife in your hand you're thinking about, but the people who'll be eating it.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: How can I cook when they aren't here?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: All your crewmates are here. If you mean the ones who obstinately continue to resist, neither of us need regret their poor choices.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: ...Tch.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: You have obtained so many things. Precious things. A kitchen, food...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Silver gave us this stuff, not you. Why're you the one preaching at me—

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Silver is dead.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: ...You killed him, didn't you?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What about us? You gonna kill us too?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: No. You are to walk the very path I did. The path of atonement.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Get any sleep?

steps.name: Worried Pirate
steps.text: I wish. I could live with the heat and the bed not shaking, but my room doesn't even get a breeze! Felt like my face was gonna turn to stone.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Count your blessings.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Look at the older mates. The wind's blown their faces right crooked. It's enough to send people running off screaming.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You're young, so you still got the chance to grow up into a real beauty.

steps.name: Worried Pirate
steps.text: I don't see any smoke from the kitchen. Is Javier still not cooking?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: I'll talk to him.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Our clerics have searched every corner of your den. There was no compass.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: ...Guess it got burnt to ash.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: The key figures in this affair—the girl who stole the compass, the graverobbing cannibal, and your former leader...

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: All have entered the depths of the Salt Flat with their ill-gotten gains.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You want us to go after them?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: You know better than I how to navigate the Flat, and you know the fugitives well.

steps.name: Eager Pirate
steps.text: How much you paying?

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: ...Excuse me?

steps.name: Eager Pirate
steps.text: We work, you pay. Isn't that supposed to be how things work around here?

steps.name: Excited Pirate
steps.text: The Flat's got a thousand ways to kill you. Massive saltfins, dozens of meters long—could tear you apart just by shaking their heads!

steps.name: Excited Pirate
steps.text: And Skeletal Reef is the worst of it. The steam blasts there could punch a hole right through you!

steps.name: Excited Pirate
steps.text: If we're risking our necks, we need a proper bounty.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Quiet, you fools! I'm sorry, we don't need—

steps.name: Eager Pirate
steps.text: What don't we need?! We've only been here a single night, so how're we supposed to put food on the table without work?!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Calm down, that's not what he meant.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You see, Señor Alguacil...

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: The caravans under inspection were carrying both coin and trade goods.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I have no use for such worldly possessions.

steps.name: Excited Pirate
steps.text: Hah, I knew they were hiding the good stuff from us!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Wait, it's not what you think—

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You heard him, mates! Do the work, get the loot. Now quit yapping and start moving!
Anastasio sees those before him as puppets of desire. Regardless of their intentions, he believes their desires will inevitably lead them down the path of evil.

a.text: 'Much like the pits of hell, the greed of man is bottomless.'

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Are you an idiot? What do you think happened to Silver?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Church conspiracies are above my pay grade. Best I can do is play the fool.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: There's no conspiracy, Rus. Silver's dead. Anastasio killed him.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: He's no schemer, but a complete lunatic. And now, there's no one to keep him in check.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You got a better idea?

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You know how the others see you. Your word as the leader isn't even worth a hot meal.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Not that you're even cooking anymore.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: I can only defend you for so long, Javier.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: ...Fine, let's board those ships.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Ugh... it's so bright...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: It hurts... everywhere...

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: You awake? You had a bit of fever last night, but it's gone down. Have some water.
Pascuala sits up and takes the bottle Teach offers her. The bionic seadragon is hard at work across the deck carrying a wooden plank while flapping its wings.
Juana stands at the bow, gazing into the distance. Behind her, Elysium twists his whole body as he strains to turn the heavy helm wheel, like some strange exercise routine.
The high sun shines bright. It hurts a little bit.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: This is our last bit of water. One pouch per person. Make it last.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: ...Is there anything I can do?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Glad to see you up and about again, chica.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Repair the hull, reinforce the mast, process the food...

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: There's plenty.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: Leaf's helping out with the repairs. Let her rest a little longer.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I lived through whatever that was yesterday, we didn't hit any skeletons all night, or get run over by a saltfin. Now I even have water to drink...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: *cough*...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: So I'm gonna do my part... to get out of this alive!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Give me your hand. I'll help you up.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: —Hyup!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Here, your water.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: And your portion of jerky. We talked about it and thought it'd be best if you focused on fixing the compass. We can worry about everything else.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: As long as we have that, we'll find our way. As for the rest, we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: How much time do we have?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: According to Señora Juana, they'll catch up to us by tomorrow morning at the latest.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: That soon? That's not nearly enough time to fix the compass.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Just do your best. If you can't get it done, she said she'll risk the Skeletal Reef, compass or not.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: And this is for you.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: A modified communicator. It'll let us talk in even the most extreme environments.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Finshit! I see sails!

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Sails! Southwest—

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You stay here. I'll go help!

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I can see their sails.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Increase speed. Catch up to them.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I wouldn't recommend that.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: And why not?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Based on their current heading, if we did, we'd only force them into the Skeletal Reef.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: What of it?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: That's no place for mere mortals! Sure, maybe they'll die in there, but we can't get in either!

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Irrelevant.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Please reconsider, Señor Alguacil. The compass'll probably get destroyed too!

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: That is not your concern.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I've sailed the Salt Flat for decades. I know how to stop a salt ship. At least let me try. It'll prevent a lot of needless deaths.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: ...Do not squander this chance, Señor Javier. You have very few left.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Javier!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...Javier!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: What are you thinking?! It's been years since we pulled off something like that, let alone against Juana!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I know it won't be enough to stop her, but forcing them to change heading is still better than herding them into Skeletal Reef.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: And if you fail? Whatever's left of your authority will be gone. You'll lose control of the fleet!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Neither will groveling to Anastasio help me keep it.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Just listen to me, one last time! Maintain a steady speed with this ship and have another go around to cut them off from the east!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Are they down a ship? Did it hit a saltfin or something?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: No one taught by me would make a mistake like that, on flat land no less.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Eyes sharp! Every last one of those salt ships is faster than this antique.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: They could easily cut us off before we make it into the Skeletal Reef.

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: What happens if they do?

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: We're at a disadvantage in both numbers and equipment. We wouldn't stand a chance.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Then we won't let them!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: The ship tailing us is going too slow and not even raising its flag. They want us to let our guard down, so another can go around in front of us.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Did you really think I would hesitate to sail into the Skeletal Reef at this point, Javier?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Full sails ahead! Set course for the Skeletal Reef! Maximum speed!

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: They're accelerating, Señor Alguacil.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: This is far from the scenario you envisioned, Señor Javier.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Raise the flag! Hail the other ship, tell them to go full sail!

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: And what of us?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I will take the helm.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Señora?! Why are you turning? This is inviting them to open fire!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: If they do, they'll have to slow down to find an angle for their cannons.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: That's our chance to lose them.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Gunners, at the ready!
Sailors heave heavy balls made from salt and fin dung into the cannons.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Fire!
Once again, Juana dances with her helm. The rudder carves through the Salt Flat, as if slicing its flesh, while the massive ship tilts and glides across the salt desert at an impossible angle.
Salt cannonballs whistle past, landing only meters from La Conquista and spraying salt everywhere.
The sails push the ancient ship towards the heart of the Flat, where few have tread.
A rumble stirs within the salt cloud. Pascuala peers through her blurry spyglass, straining to identify its source, only for a wind-filled sail to suddenly consume her view.
It is the salt ship that has disappeared from the pursuing squadron.
Pascuala puts down her spyglass with a jolt as the salt ship, trailing a billowing cloud of salt dust, barrels straight toward them!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: It's gonna hit us!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Evasive maneuvers! Evasive maneuvers!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: No! That's what they want—for us to slow down or turn!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: The main sails of that ship are at the bow! It's not designed for ramming!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Let them try! If they do, they'll never catch us again!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Forward!
Hruff—!
The sound of canvas straining in the wind fills everyone's ears as La Conquista charges on, evading the salt ship's interception.
For the first time in decades, it rides proudly at the head of the fleet again.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You're out of your mind, Juana!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: You should have known that the moment you mutinied!

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: Catch them.

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: Javier!

steps.name: Rus
steps.text: ...Fine. I'll take command! Full sail ahead!
Javier stops giving orders. He knows no one will listen anymore.
He passes through the crowd and climbs the ship's bow. He sees the towering skeletons just ahead of La Conquista.
The Skeletal Reef: a labyrinth of bones, the pulsing heart of the Salt Flat, a realm of death where no mortal dares tread. Yet, La Conquista sails toward its valleys, dauntlessly, recklessly.
Despite the constant bumps and jolts, Isidro's eyes remain fixed on the Corazonix floating at the center of the transmutation table.
Layers of Arts energy fields have separated it. The insides glow with a metallic gleam.
Even the slightest motion is reflected upon its surface through the needle of the probe.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: The rusted alloy has been successfully isolated. The newly added alloy has been successfully integrated.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Now, for the last step, to etch a new Originium circuit inside the Corazonix... I can't afford to make a single mistake.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: There is no time to test the effects of the circuit. We have only one chance.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Steady, steady...
Another jolt sends the dismantled compass components on the table spilling onto the ground.
With one hand holding the probe, Isidro draws his sword with the other and stabs the cabin wall with it to steady himself.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: El Dominio del Mar... If the pirates can fight in the wind and waves with this technique, then I can use it to steady myself amidst this turbulence!
With each tilt of the ship, Isidro counters with a thrust of his sword. Soon, the cabin is in chaos—a pot covers one of his feet, while a piece of canvas wraps around his leg.
He pays no heed to them. The only thing he sees is the trail of liquid Originium drawn by the needle of his probe.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Almost there...
Sweat runs down his cheeks and into his mouth. He feels control slipping from the hand holding the probe as his strained muscles verge on spasming.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I did it! I did it!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Now, all that's left is to insert the shaped Corazonix back into the shell of the compass...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: —Argh!
Isidro forces his eyelids open through the blood and salt, and sees the Arts field beginning to go out of control under some kind of powerful Arts interference.
His probe lies on the other side of the cabin, the needle broken into several pieces. The components of the compass are nowhere to be seen, except for the outer shell.
Under the pressure of the overloaded Arts field, the newly-formed Corazonix begins to tremble violently.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Thorns! Thorns!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: What did that finshit Anastasio just do?!

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: *cough* An Inquisition handcannon. He fired it into the cabin!

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Stay away from the alchemical equipment! It's out of control because of interference from the handcannon's Arts energy!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: What are you doing here, Señora Juana? Who has the helm?

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Don't worry, it's in good hands.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Teach! Where's Teach?!

steps.name: Weedy
steps.text: She's over here! She's got a piece of broken wood stuck in her leg!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Damn it... damn it! I can't stop the bleeding!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Thorns! Thorns! Say something!
Isidro opens his mouth, but his tongue does not obey. He forces himself to sit up. There is no time to think about how many ribs he broke.
On the transmutation table, the Corazonix starts to bubble as if it's boiling.
One moment of hesitation, and the last Corazonix of Iberia, their only hope for survival—
Will turn to dust.
He must retrieve it!
Isidro looks around desperately, but sees none of the compass's components, not even a working tool.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: No... no...
Isidro stumbles to his feet. He cannot feel his left arm, but can still move his right arm.
He runs towards the transmutation table.
The resistance from the Arts field is much stronger than expected. It feels like putting his hand into boiling magma.
His glove offers no protection against the rampaging Arts energy. Isidro quivers as the energy corrodes his arm.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: What are you doing, Thorns?!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: This is my Corazonix.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...MY compass!
The Corazonix dances in his palm, as though it has gained life.
It flows through every gash and hole the Arts energy left upon his arm.
Isidro has gazed upon this substance so many times, seeking a connection with it.
But now, in this very moment, he understands that it has become one with his flesh.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Argh—!!
